  "text": "The boy opened his hand. There was a pale band around his middle finger, but no ring.

“I didn't take it,” he said. “I only thought about it.”

The woman pushed the copper coins together with the side of her shoe.

“That's usually enough.”

He pulled his sleeve free and went to the cupboard. The door would open no farther than the width of his hand. Something soft resisted it near the bottom.

“Anne?”

“Don't push. That's my foot.”

He knelt. Through the gap he could see a slipper, blue once, with the stitching repaired in white cotton. He had bought her those slippers at the hospital shop because she'd complained about the cold floor.

“You were buried in those.”

“Well,” she said, “I couldn't find the others.”

On the landing, the footsteps stopped.

The woman picked up her stone.

“Ask her what happened to the ring.”

He kept his eyes on the slipper. “What happened to it?”

“I gave it back.”

“To whom?”

No answer came from the cupboard. Instead, above him, a hand slid down the banister. He watched its fingers pass over the place where he had left the ring.

It was his hand. The little finger had the same crooked joint, broken years ago in a car door.

The boy began separating the coins again.

“I said give it to me,” he whispered.

The woman stepped aside, leaving room at the foot of the stairs.

From behind the cupboard door, Anne said, “Don't let him tell you you've had your turn.”"
